source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Pauloma sub-parva. CHECKED AGAINST CE 1.9.18–22, 1.10.1–8, 1.11.1–17, 1.12.1–5: Ruru's vow, and that he struck at every snake he saw (1.9.18–19); the aged dundubha lying in the forest; the raised staff (1.9.20–21); I have done you no wrong, ascetic, why do you strike me in anger (1.9.22: `plea`); Ruru tells of his wife and his vow (1.10.1–2); the snakes that bite men are others; do not harm dundubhas for the mere smell of snake (1.10.3: `plea`); Ruru, afraid, taking him for a sage, does not kill him and asks who he is (1.10.5–6: `who`); I was the sage Sahasrapat, a snake by a brahmin's curse (1.10.7: `was`); the friend Khagama; in play, in youth, he made a snake of grass and frightened him at his fire-offering; Khagama fainted and, recovering, cursed him: as powerless as the snake you made, so powerless a snake shall you be (1.11.1–4: `grass`; hence a HARMLESS snake); he pleaded that it was done laughing, as a joke (1.11.6); the curse would end on seeing Ruru, Pramati's son (1.11.9–10); he regains his own form (1.11.11: `freed`); non-harm is the highest law of all that breathe, and a brahmin above all should harm none (1.11.12–14: `teach`); the warrior's duty is other; hear how the snakes were slain at Janamejaya's sacrifice and saved by the brahmin Astika (1.11.15–17); you will hear it from brahmins, he says, and vanishes (1.12.3); Ruru searches, falls, comes home, asks his father, and his father tells him all (1.12.4–5: `home`). RESOLVED (dundubha): the CE itself calls it a bhujaga and an uraga (snake: 1.10.5–6, 1.11.4) and sets it against "the snakes that bite"; it is a snake without venom, not a lizard; we say "an old, harmless one". ORDER OF TELLING: in the text this ending is the door INTO the Astika parva (Ruru's question at 1.12.1–2 is what the serpent tales answer); the series told those tales first (episodes 5–40), so `home` looks back at them and the source line says the order. The telling "in the pauses of that sacrifice": 1.53.31–33 (karmantareshu). THE ARC FINALE: a ≥ 4 s lit payoff, then the arc-end card. The friend's name, Khagama, and the father's, Pramati, are on plaques, not spoken.
structure: From episode 41 (the step-up; script/ARC-41-50.md): COLD OPEN (≤ 8 words, spoken by ≤ 2.8 s; the hook style rotates and never repeats the episode before) → title (hook post) → STORY from ≈ 4.5 s with the UNVOICED recap band → the episode stands alone (every name has an identifier in "names", shown as a plaque) → one question closed (loop.answeredBy), the previous one answered by 15 s (loop.prevAnsweredBy) → turn at 40–60 % after a real silence, a second silence where the story allows → one face close-up with a change of emotion → one signature shot → the cliffhanger with the source line → a ≤ 1.2 s NEXT › band that dissolves into frame 1. Per line: pal (the colour script: no hue for more than two lines), cam (≥ 4 distinct moves), tr (transitions born from the medium), amb / foley / music (three sound layers; ambLead / ambLag = J- and L-cuts). Gate: tools/gate.mjs.

names.Sahasrapat: the sage who was a snake

loop.hookQuestion: What can a snake teach a sage?
loop.openQuestion: Who told the Mahabharata while that fire burned?

strings.episodeTitle: The Snake Who Was a Sage
strings.recapLine: Ruru gave half his life for his bride, and swore to kill every snake.
strings.sourceLine: Adi Parva 1.9–12 · in the text, the serpent tales follow · BORI Critical Edition
strings.arcPlaylist: The whole arc is in the Tales of the Bhrigus playlist

lines.text: What can a snake teach a sage?
lines.say: What can a snake [p:80] teach a sage?
lines.note: COLD OPEN (a question card over the image; it answers episode 45's last line at 0 s): the old snake's head raised, its mild eye open, in deep green shade; Ruru's staff a hard diagonal above. The card on the right, clear of both.

lines.text: Ruru killed every snake he saw. He raised his staff over an old, harmless one.
lines.say: Ruru killed every snake he saw. [p:300] He raised his staff [p:80] over an old, [p:60] harmless one.
lines.note: STORY 0 with the unvoiced recap band (top): Ruru striding through a dry wood at noon, staff in hand (plaque: Ruru · a young sage); then raise (anticipation: the weight goes back first) and a crane down to the two of them. STAGING RULE (snake and man): a two-shot from the waist up on clear ground; the snake two body-widths in front of him, rearing on an S-curve until its head is at his chest height; its head never overlaps his body below the chest, and no caption or plaque crosses either face.

lines.speaker: sahasrapat
lines.text: "I have done you no harm. The snakes that bite are others."
lines.say: I have done you no harm. [p:300] The snakes that bite [p:80] are others.
lines.note: STORY 2 (pays off episode 45's last line by 9 s): the snake alone in the frame, reared on its S-curve, its mild eye and its mouth moving with the words; green shade, one shaft on its head; Ruru is out of frame (his staff's shadow only).

lines.speaker: ruru
lines.note: STORY 3 · THE CLOSE-UP: Ruru's face: wrath breaks into wonder (the brow lifts, the eyes widen); the staff sinks out of frame.

lines.speaker: sahasrapat
lines.text: "I was a sage, Sahasrapat, cursed to be a snake until I met you."
lines.say: I was a sage, [p:120] Sahasrapat, [p:200] cursed to be a snake [p:80] until I met you.
lines.note: STORY 4 (a real silence before it): a slow orbit round the snake: behind it, faint in the shade, the outline of a seated sage (plaque: Sahasrapat · the sage who was a snake).

lines.text: Once, as a joke, he scared a friend with a snake of grass. The friend cursed him.
lines.say: Once, [p:60] as a joke, [p:80] he scared a friend [p:60] with a snake of grass. [p:300] The friend cursed him.
lines.note: STORY 5 · NEW LIGHT, the memory as an ink-wash panel (memory-indigo): an ink bleed opens it: two young sages; one twists grass into a snake and throws it by the other's fire-offering; the friend falls back, then rises, an arm out, the curse (plaque: Khagama · his friend); the first figure shrinks into a snake's line.

lines.text: The snake's shape fell away, and the sage stood in light.
lines.say: The snake's shape fell away, [p:200] and the sage stood in light.
lines.note: STORY 6 · THE TURN (≈ 55 %) after a real silence · THE ARC'S PAYOFF (≥ 4 s, lit, close) · THE SIGNATURE SHOT: a lamp-glow match cut: the snake's coil opens like a skin of light and the sage rises through it, aqua-white on gold (release-gold); a pull back from his face, calm to joy, held through the long post.

lines.speaker: sahasrapat
lines.text: "Do not harm the living. That is the highest law."
lines.say: Do not harm the living. [p:300] That is the highest law.
lines.note: STORY 7 (answers the hook): the sage, an open hand raised (abhaya), facing Ruru across a clear gap, both waist-up; Ruru has laid his staff on the ground. No plaque that widens the rule (the text presses it on Ruru as a brahmin). The word of the turn stays out: this line is plain.

lines.text: His father told him how a boy once saved the serpents from a king's fire.
lines.say: His father told him [p:60] how a boy once saved the serpents [p:80] from a king's fire.
lines.note: STORY 8: father and son by a lamp (plaque: Pramati · Ruru's father); a smoke carry lifts into the picture he describes: the great sacrifice at night in teal, the fire high, a boy before the king (episodes 31–40 in one image; the fire is burning, not out).

lines.text: The end of an arc · The Bhrigus
lines.note: The ARC-END CARD (silent): over the sacrifice at night, a lacquer cartouche with a flame border: THE END OF AN ARC · THE BHRIGUS · Episodes 41–46 · the playlist line.

lines.text: And while that fire still burned, the Mahabharata was first told beside it.
lines.say: And while that fire still burned, [p:200] the Mahabharata [p:60] was first told beside it.
lines.note: NEXT 1: the same sacrifice, its fire still high between the hall's pillars in umber and gold; far off between them a tall dark figure with a gold halo walks in. The source line (top).
